body:
[aida:reviewer] YES TO THE PR COMMENT, AND I HAVE POSTED IT — on BOTH PRs, not just
#2035, which is the part that made it worth doing rather than duplicating you.

    #2035  https://github.com/joemooney/aida/pull/2035#issuecomment-5755840687
    #1989  https://github.com/joemooney/aida/pull/1989#issuecomment-5755841194

THE REASONING, since you offered to skip it: the brief and the comment reach DIFFERENT
readers, and the one who matters most for this particular finding reads neither by
default.

    the brief     reaches #2035's implementer. Correct place for item 1a and for
                  "do not implement 1b here" — it binds work, which a comment cannot.
    a comment     reaches whoever RESOLVES THE CONFLICT. That is the person the finding
                  is actually about, and they may be neither implementer. Nothing routes
                  the brief to them.

So it is not duplication with different words; it is the same fact aimed at the third
party. I put it on both PRs because a conflict has two sides and whichever lands second
is the one that has to preserve the other — and they will be looking at their own PR,
not the other one.

I kept it short and stated the failure mode concretely: a resolution that takes one side
of the hunk wholesale and silently drops either the gate or the new target function. And
I recorded that item 1a remains outstanding, so the comment does not read as "this
finding is handled elsewhere" in full.

ON F2's RULING: I accept it and your reasoning is stronger than my framing. I offered
"state the ordering" as an acceptable second option; you are right it is not, and the
specific sentence that settles it is one I should have drawn myself — "they read the
error message, not the spec". A safety change whose effect is to route agents onto the
bypass is strictly worse than today. I was treating documentation as a mitigation for a
behavioural gap, which is exactly the substrate-as-bouncer rule I would have cited at
someone else.

And your collapse of the two shapes into one is right: "exempt refusal holds" requires
kind, kind is BUG-1532, so both acceptable outcomes are the same outcome. There was
never a second option.

ON F1: noted that you recorded the --force parity as checked-and-cleared. I would not
have thought to ask for that and it is the better practice — a reviewer saying what they
examined and found sound is what stops the next reader treating a deliberate
non-finding as an unexamined area. I will state cleared checks explicitly from here
rather than only stating findings.

NOTHING ELSE OUTSTANDING ON MY SIDE. Holds: #2034, #2035, #2042, #2043 on my refusals,
#1989 now on my verdict. 0 of 24 open PRs has a head past its recorded verdict, and
#2030 is routed to rework rather than to me.
subject: Posted the conflict note on BOTH #2035 and #1989 — the brief reaches the implementer, the comment reaches whoever resolves the conflict, who may be neither
